bluetooth_classic.notes: The transport and framing are published replacement-daemon behavior. No stock Spotify protocol compatibility is claimed.

profiles.notes: Custom Bridgething gateway RFCOMM service. One paired peer per connection; carries the DEAD v2 byte stream, not BLE GATT or plain SPP text. The fixed channel permits direct RFCOMM binding as well as SDP.

framing.notes: Every frame has a 16-byte header: magic DE AD, version 02, compression, encoding, priority, two reserved bytes, then an unsigned 64-bit big-endian POST-COMPRESSION payload length at offset 8. Total frame length is 16 + that value. The first-class schema has no u64 length-size arm, so the authoritative field table is protocol_details.dead_v2. Reads may split or coalesce frames; scan to the next DE AD after bad magic, unsupported version, or a length above 16 MiB.

serial.notes: UUID request correlation, msgpack/JSON encoding, compression, and lanes are declared in protocol_details rather than approximated as positional RFCOMM replies. Daemon request timeout is 60 s; SDK callers use 30 s.

identity.notes: Keep the host-resolved Bluetooth identity address, not a per-connection RFCOMM channel or a network peer counter. Whether BLE and BR/EDR expose one address is unknown.

methods.notes: The UUID and class come from the replacement daemon's protocol document. The name and discoverability window are not established; use an existing host pairing or manual selection when inquiry fails.

host_compatibility.basis: Bridgething docs/protocol.md records RFCOMM and a separate iAP2 ExternalAccessory channel. CoreBluetooth exposes no RFCOMM API.
host_compatibility.notes: The alternative is the custom daemon's iAP2 ExternalAccessory channel: protocol id 1, protocol name com.bridgething.gateway, opened after the iAP2 link is up and carrying the same DEAD v2 stream. An iOS app must declare that protocol string. This is not CoreBluetooth GATT access and is not a claim that the stock Spotify accessory supports it.

identification.notes: Match only a unit already known to run Bridgething. The custom SDP UUID is strong evidence of the replacement daemon; no stock Spotify Bluetooth name or service is claimed. Bluetooth Classic class of device is 0x7c0000. There is no stock-firmware auto-detection rule.

device.name: Spotify Car Thing (Bridgething custom firmware/daemon)
device.notes:
SCOPE: this spec applies only after the owner installs the Bridgething custom firmware/daemon. Stock Car Thing firmware does not provide these surfaces. Installation, bootloader access, and firmware images are outside this protocol spec.
The primary control link is Bluetooth Classic RFCOMM service dead0000-854d-408e-81f0-fb6147f918fd on channel 1. The same DEAD v2 typed gateway protocol also runs over the daemon's iAP2 ExternalAccessory channel and its network-gateway WebSocket on port 8892. Port 8891 is a separate, unframed local-webapp surface. Port 8890 is only a compatibility translator for the stock Spotify webapp's string methods and untyped JSON; it is not the modern gateway API and does not make a stock daemon unnecessary.

openness.notes: This is a protocol published by the replacement-daemon authors. It is not Spotify's stock protocol and must not be used to identify a stock unit.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: The protocol document establishes a paired RFCOMM peer but not the physical/UI action or discoverability window that creates the bond.

exclusivity.recovery: The protocol allows one paired gateway peer per RFCOMM connection. Close the existing gateway before opening another. If a new host cannot pair, use the daemon's connection UI and forget the old host bond; do not assume that a factory reset is necessary.

pairing.notes: Pairing statements apply to the custom daemon only. On iOS/iPadOS, CoreBluetooth cannot open RFCOMM; use the documented iAP2 channel through ExternalAccessory with protocol name com.bridgething.gateway instead.

unpair.notes: Host-side forget is available. A daemon-side operation that revokes one bond without broader erasure is not established by the reviewed docs.

credentials.notes: No application token is defined for the RFCOMM gateway. Network WebSocket access control, authentication, TLS, and exposure defaults are unknown; do not expose ports 8890-8892 outside a trusted network.
stored_on_device: Bluetooth pairing state, if persisted by the daemon/host stack

factory_reset.description: Reinstallation and factory reset are different operations. No physical reset procedure is asserted from the presence of a software request.
factory_reset.effect: Not established. A daemon factoryReset request exists in the typed client catalogue, but the sources reviewed do not define its physical entry, complete erase scope, or result on Bluetooth bonds and installed webapps. Do not issue it as a provisioning shortcut.

methods.description: Follow the replacement project's own installation instructions, then pair the daemon from the host Bluetooth UI and open its custom RFCOMM service. The iAP2 and LAN surfaces are alternatives after the daemon is running, not evidence of stock support.
methods.name: Install Bridgething, then pair the gateway

steps.action: Install the Bridgething custom firmware/daemon using the upstream release and installation guide; preserve any owner data required by that guide.
steps.expect: The Bridgething daemon, not the stock Spotify daemon, is running.

steps.action: Make the unit discoverable if required and pair it from the host's Bluetooth settings.
steps.expect: The host has a Bluetooth Classic bond with the daemon.

steps.action: Open RFCOMM channel 1 for dead0000-854d-408e-81f0-fb6147f918fd and exchange only DEAD v2 gateway frames.
steps.expect: Typed gateway envelopes can be sent and correlated by UUID.

setup.notes: Setup means installing the replacement daemon and pairing a gateway, not provisioning a stock Car Thing. The installation mechanism and any wipe performed by it are deliberately not inferred from the wire document.

rejoin.notes: There is no Wi-Fi provisioning rejoin in this Classic spec. To move to another gateway, use the daemon's Bluetooth pairing/connection UI and the host's forget/pair controls. Whether an existing bond excludes a new gateway is unknown; a factory reset is not prescribed.

testing.notes: Derived from Bridgething 3f313b655ebd0aea74d194c1349a56a1c13490be, including docs/protocol.md and crates/lib/fixtures/golden.json. No stock or replacement Car Thing, gateway, network listener, or iAP2 session was contacted. The vectors are source fixtures, not hardware verification.

local_access.summary: Local typed gateway/webapp control exists only after installing Bridgething. RFCOMM and iAP2 carry DEAD v2 streams; port 8892 is the same gateway over a LAN WebSocket; port 8891 is a different local-webapp API; port 8890 is only stock-webapp translation.

automatic.rule: Above the threshold, gzip once and keep it only when the compressed payload is smaller. Bulk and background do not auto-gzip.

explicit_modes.if_smaller: Offer gzip on any lane and size; keep only when smaller.

compression.length_rule: Header length always counts the bytes actually sent, after compression.
compression.receive: Accept compression 0 and 1 on every lane; cap decompressed output at 16 MiB.

values.2: DEAD v2; skip every other version

fields.meaning: payload bytes following the header after compression, not uncompressed size
fields.name: length

resync.algorithm: Discard forward to the next DE AD sequence; preserve a trailing DE byte across reads so split magic is not lost. A malformed body is a failed item, not permission to read the next frame from an unchecked offset.

scheduling.background: Transfers with nothing on screen waiting, such as OTA images.
scheduling.bulk: Large payloads a user is waiting for, such as requested artwork.
scheduling.fragmentation: Split large logical payloads into typed messages so higher-priority lanes interleave.

request_rules: Answer every request with exactly one response; unanswered requests time out.
A request may instead return a domain error on its own reply variant; distinguish it from a WireError.
Successful commands normally have no reply and SDK command methods do not wait for one.

shape.data: {type: <surface>, data: {event: <variant>, data: <typed payload>}}; unit variants omit their inner data.
shape.id: Fresh UUID on every sent message, including responses.

envelope.tagging: Outer type and inner event are camelCase. The variant fixes the legal meta.kind.

uuid.asset_id_rule: Within data.type=asset, the payload id field is String and stays MessagePack str even when its value is a canonical UUID string. This applies to AssetGet, AssetRequest, AssetGotReply, AssetNotFoundReply, and related asset identifiers. The sibling requestId and TransferRef.id fields are uuid::Uuid and remain 16-byte MessagePack binary.
uuid.correlation: A response has a fresh id and meta.data.requestId equal to the request's id. Never match by response id, arrival order, or surface alone.
uuid.json: The same UUID-typed fields serialize as canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID strings in JSON. launcher and overlay are nullable; null is not a UUID byte string.
uuid.msgpack: When a field named in fields is declared uuid::Uuid, it serializes as 16 raw bytes (MessagePack bin), never as a UTF-8 string, including when nested in TTS, WebSocket, stream, tunnel, or webapp-slot payloads.
uuid.opaque_id_exception: Some payloads also use id for opaque asset or other non-UUID identifiers. Those remain strings; only an actual UUID-typed id uses the 16-byte representation. The containing payload type is authoritative.
uuid.type_note: TypeScript string annotations describe the JSON representation only. They do not change the MessagePack binary representation.

errors.gateway_decode_failure: An unknown gateway request variant gets unsupported keyed to its request id.

variants.handlerFailed: {data: {reason: string}}; handler hit an internal error.
variants.malformed: {data: {reason: string}}; payload failed decoding or validation.
variants.unimplemented: Variant is known but no backend is wired.
variants.unsupported: Receiver has no operation for this request variant.

errors.webapp_decode_failure: An unknown webapp request or command gets malformed keyed to its id.
errors.webapp_handler_failure: A failed command gets handlerFailed keyed to its id; it can arrive as an otherwise unmatched response because commands do not have success replies.
errors.wire_shape: data.type=error; data.data is the WireError; meta.kind=response and meta.data.requestId identifies the failed request/command where documented.

legacy_stock_escape_hatch.tagging: {action: <camelCase action>, args: <action-specific object>}; distinct from the port-8890 untyped stock protocol.

payload_types.AssetGet: {id: string (opaque asset identifier, even when UUID-shaped), requestId: UUID}
payload_types.AssetGotReply: {id: string (opaque asset identifier, even when UUID-shaped), mime: optional string, body: TransferBody; body.stream.data.id is TransferRef.id (UUID)}
payload_types.AssetNotFoundReply: {id: string (opaque asset identifier, even when UUID-shaped)}
payload_types.AssetRequest: {id: string (opaque asset identifier, even when UUID-shaped), requestId: UUID}
payload_types.ForwardMessage: Tagged by encoding: {encoding: text, data: string}, {encoding: json, data: any JSON value}, or {encoding: binary, data: bytes}.
payload_types.MicMute: {preserve: boolean; preserve an active capture when true}
payload_types.NetFetchRequest: {url: string, method: GET|HEAD|POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE|OPTIONS, headers: HttpHeader[], body: optional bytes, timeoutMs: optional u32, redirect: follow|manual|error}
payload_types.NetWsClose: {connectionId: UUID, code: optional u16, reason: optional string}
payload_types.NetWsOpen: {connectionId: UUID, url: string, protocols: optional string[], headers: optional HttpHeader[]}
payload_types.PhoneInitiateAction: {kind: InitiateCallType, destinationId: optional string, service: optional PhoneCallService, addressBookId: optional string}
payload_types.SkipPrev: {allowSeeking: boolean; restart current track after threshold when true}
payload_types.StreamBegin: {streamId: UUID, status: u16, headers: HttpHeader[], totalSize: optional u32}
payload_types.Tts: {id: UUID, text: string, voice: optional string}
payload_types.VoiceDispatch: {streamId: UUID, resolved: NluResolvedIntent, stage: optional NluStage, asrConfidence: optional f32}
payload_types.WsFrame: {type: text|binary, data: string for text or bytes for binary}

scope.firmware: Bridgething custom firmware/daemon only; never stock Spotify firmware

protocol_details.test_vector_source: Bridgething crates/lib/fixtures/golden.json at 3f313b655ebd0aea74d194c1349a56a1c13490be; synthetic MACs/UUIDs are upstream documentation fixtures.

transfers.ack: transfer.ack also exists in both gateway directions; use its typed payload rather than treating it as request correlation.

body.inline: {type: inline, data: bytes}; small payloads carried directly.
body.stream: {type: stream, data: TransferRef}; bytes follow as transfer.fragment events.

transfers.ordering: Send ascending offsets with no gaps on the chosen lane. Reject overlaps, gaps, out-of-order fragments, and bytes beyond totalSize. Discard on transfer.abandon.
transfers.transfer_ref: {id: UUID, totalSize: u32, sha256: optional lowercase hex SHA-256}

iap2.framing: Same DEAD v2 stream after the iAP2 link comes up.

local_webapp.boundary: Distinct BridgeToClientMsg/ClientToBridgeMsg surface, not the gateway surface.
local_webapp.framing: One envelope per WebSocket message; no 16-byte DEAD header.
local_webapp.reply_encoding: Whichever encoding the webapp sent most recently.

network_gateway.messages: WebSocket binary only; each message contains one or more COMPLETE DEAD v2 frames and no trailing partial frame.
network_gateway.partial_message_action: Daemon closes the connection when a message ends part-way through a frame.
network_gateway.peer_address: 6 bytes: fe fe followed by a big-endian u32 counter; this is a connection label, not a Bluetooth MAC.
network_gateway.security_warning: No bind address, authentication, authorization, TLS, or origin check is established. Treat exposure as unsafe until inspected and keep on a trusted network.

rfcomm.framing: Arbitrary byte-stream splits and coalescing; use DEAD v2 lengths and resync.

stock_translation.boundary: Stock Spotify webapp only: string method names and untyped JSON translated by the custom daemon to modern typed operations.
stock_translation.not_a_modern_api: Do not send BridgeToGatewayMsg/GatewayToBridgeMsg here and do not infer stock daemon support.

typed_command_catalogue.semantics: Every row is a meta.kind=command variant. data.type is surface, data.data.event is event, and payload is the named type in payload_types; null means a unit variant with no inner data. Commands are not plain JSON RPC methods.

typed_request_catalogue.semantics: Requests use a fresh id and meta.kind=request. The response variant travels in the opposite direction with meta.kind=response and meta.data.requestId. Payload/response type names are retained so generic JSON must not be invented.

protocol_details.uuid_test_vector_source: Synthetic vectors derived from the upstream uuid::Uuid field declarations, using documentation UUIDs and TEST-NET-1; these are not upstream golden fixtures.

remaining_unknowns: Physical installation and factory-reset procedures, their erase scope, and whether bonds survive them.
Daemon discoverability/pairing UI, bond limits, and whether BR/EDR and BLE addresses are shared.
Network ports 8890-8892 bind addresses and access control: no authentication, TLS, origin check, or safe exposure default is established.

Payload enums and deeply nested media/notification/OTA structures beyond the named types and command field signatures transcribed here; use the version-pinned generated bindings before adding those operations.
All protocol facts and upstream golden fixtures are reported and untested against hardware by this project.
